A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZS-NCD research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated proofs, experiments, and visual comparisons can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original denoising experiments, PSNR/SSIM results, ablations, and image reconstructions in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds comparisons with DS-N2N and Pixel2Pixel in Appendix B.2, Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the compression-weight selection procedure: fixed doubling/halving becomes residual-dependent multiplicative adjustment, the update direction above the noise target reverses, and tolerance-based termination is added. The network architecture, training objective, quantization approach, and patch aggregation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Set11, Set13, Kodak24, Mouse Nuclei, and PolyU under the same noise scenarios. Unknown-parameter Poisson denoising already appears in v1 Appendix A.2; its appearance in v2 Section 4 is a relocation.

E2.justification: v2 adds DS-N2N and Pixel2Pixel as evaluated competitors on Kodak24 under both AWGN and Poisson noise, substantially updating the comparison with recent zero-shot methods (Appendix B.2, Tables 5–6). Existing comparisons remain. N2F is newly cited but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported crops, noise levels, PSNR/SSIM metrics, training budgets, dataset-specific compression weights, and baseline-best versus ZS-NCD-final iteration policy remain unchanged. The new Kodak24 comparisons use the existing noise conditions. No experimental-setting revision is reported to explain the changed BM3D scores.

E4.justification: The compression-weight sensitivity, Conv-versus-MLP, patch aggregation, patch-size/downsampling, and MSE-versus-NLL analyses retain their evidence and findings. The Poisson-parameter estimation example and calibration table also existed in v1; their relocation does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Cross-image averaging remains unchanged. Changes to theoretical probability bounds belong to T1.

E6.justification: New baseline results establish mixed Poisson rankings: at Kodak24 alpha=25, Pixel2Pixel achieves 29.26 dB versus ZS-NCD's retained 28.77 dB, while ZS-NCD leads the added AWGN comparisons. BM3D's Set11 AWGN averages also change: 30.83/0.8659 becomes 29.79/0.8523 at sigma=25, and 28.25/0.8049 becomes 26.56/0.7619 at sigma=50 (v1 Tables 1/6; v2 Tables 2/8). These are revised comparator results, not gains in ZS-NCD's retained scores.

T1.justification: Corollary 1 replaces the l2-bounded sparse class with an linfinity-bounded class, revises the error and probability bounds, and replaces the covering-number proof with support coding and coordinate quantization (v2 Appendix A.3). Lemma 2's admissible upper limit for t changes from 2 sigma_n squared/(3 w_M) to 3 sigma_n squared/(2 w_M). The Taylor remainder in Lemma 1 changes from plus to minus, introducing a sign error. These are substantive changes beyond proof relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and central conclusion retain the claims of single-image compression-based denoising, resistance to overfitting, finite-sample Gaussian/Poisson guarantees, and state-of-the-art performance. The concluding fixed-code qualification reiterates a distinction already stated in v1 Section 4.

C2.justification: Remark 1 weakens the assertion that MSE incurs no performance loss relative to ML to the statement that both can recover the signal. Section 4 explicitly qualifies residual matching by a low-noise regime. The sparse-signal discussion replaces the MMSE-dimension analogy with a claimed minimax-rate connection and discussion of the residual 2/n term.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 identifies the official implementations as the source of the new baseline results. Algorithm 1 exposes tolerance and damping controls, although tested numerical values are not supplied. Existing architecture details, hardware, runtimes, optimizer schedules, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to N2F, DS-N2N, and Pixel2Pixel and explains the latter two methods in Appendix B.2. The sparse-signal discussion replaces Wu and Verdu's MMSE dimension reference with Johnstone's Gaussian estimation text. The broader positioning of neural compression for zero-shot denoising remains intact.

P1.justification: The full proof section moves from the main text to Appendix A, with the corollary proof reordered after Theorem 1's proof. Poisson-parameter estimation moves into Section 4, and the conclusion now follows the experiments directly. This substantially reorganizes the narrative, alongside targeted rewrites and clearer appendix headings.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–6, moves the Poisson calibration table into the main text, enlarges Figure 4, and converts the wrapped Conv/MLP comparison into a standalone table. Other displays receive resizing and caption edits. Existing heatmaps and reconstruction images are retained.

improvement.justification: Recent-baseline comparisons, a more direct main narrative, and the more cautious Poisson interpretation improve v2. However, Appendix A.1.1 introduces an incorrect Taylor-remainder sign in Equation 15, and Lemma 2 expands its stated range without adapting the proof's parameter constraint. Because theoretical support is central to the paper, these benefits and mathematical regressions prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
